question.text: A helicopter takes off along the vertical with an acceleration <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and zero initial velocity. In a certain time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, the pilot switches off the engine. At the point of take-off, the sound dies away in time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. Determine the velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> of the helicopter (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>) at the moment when its engine is switched off, assuming that the velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> of sound is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>320</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
